segments.text: Good afternoon. This is Aakashwani and I am Valsa Williams with the Midday News.
The headlines
Prime Minister Narendra Modi says solar power, a key driver of clean energy transition, to
meet growing energy needs. Government notifies grievance redressal rules for VBG-ROMG scheme.
The Ministry of Defence inks contracts with defence public sector undertakings worth
53,800 crore rupees for eight next-generation Corvettes for the Indian Navy.
Severe Cyclonic Storm Murasu to hit South Andhra Pradesh coast tonight, state government intensifies
preparedness.
And Italian Kimi Antonelli becomes Formula One's youngest world champion at 20 years.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi today said India's clean energy transition is gathering pace,
with solar power playing a growing role in meeting the country's energy needs.
Mr Modi said this while sharing an article written by Union Minister of New and Renewable
Energy Prahlad Joshi and founder of Bloomberg LP Michael R. Bloomberg.
The Prime Minister noted that the article stresses on the growth of renewable energy,
energy, the expansion of rooftop solar and investments in storage and transmission.
It also highlighted how this shift is helping reduce electricity bills, create jobs and
strengthen energy security.
Prime Minister Modi will inaugurate the Bharat Renewable Energy Summit and Expo 2026 at
Bharat Mandapur, New Delhi today.
He will also address the gathering on the occasion the four-day summit will be held
till the fifth of this month.
Hence, the theme of the summit is Invest, Innovate, Inspire, more from our correspondent.
The Bharat Renewal Energy Summit and Export 2026 will attract participants from over 130
countries, including more than 40 ministers along with policymakers, investors, financial
institutions and industry leaders.
It will serve as a global platform for clean energy investment, industry engagement and
technology partnerships.
The summit is witnessing the participation from Australia, Denmark, the European Union,
France, Germany, the Netherlands, Norway, Sweden and the UK as country partners.
The summit is being held alongside the 9th session of the International Solar Alliance
Assembly and the 4th International Conference on Green Hydrogen.
The summit will also host plenary sessions, ministerial discussions and government-to-government
engagement to promote investment, partnerships and project development.
Meanwhile, the expo will feature over 400 exhibitors showcasing advanced technologies,
Indian manufacturing capabilities and clean energy solutions across solar and wind power,
green hydrogen, energy storage and other emerging areas.
With Summert's report, Payal Sharma, Akashwani News, Delhi.
The government has notified the Vikesit Bharat Guarantee for Rosgarh and RGB Commission
Gramine, VBG Ramji, grievance redressal rules, 2026 establishing a structured multi-tier
and time-bound mechanism for addressing grievances relating to the implementation of the scheme.
The Ministry of Rural Development said the rules aim to make grievance redressal more accessible,
transparent and accountable, while ensuring that citizens' concerns receive timely attention
action and appropriate action, a report.
The ministry said that the rules provide for the establishment of a time-bound multi-tier
grievance redressal mechanism by state governments at the Gram Panchayat block and district levels.
It said that designated grievance redressal officers at the appropriate levels will be
responsible for receiving, registering, inquiring into and disposing of grievances.
To facilitate easy access, any person may submit a grievance relating to any matter
are rising out of or connected with the implementation of the scheme.
The rules provide for submission of grievances in person before the designated
Grievance Redressal Officer through speed post with proof of delivery through
the digital public infrastructure for the Dressal of Grievances designated by
the central government and through telephone. The rules also prescribe
clear timelines to ensure prompt examination and resolution of
grievances. The enquiry into a grievance is required to be completed within 7 working
days and resolved within 15 days from the date of its
reception. With Anupam Mishra, Rishu Jaiswal, Aakashmare News, Delhi.
The Ministry of Defence today signed contracts worth over 53,800 crore rupees with garden
reach, shipbuilders and engineers limited and Goa shipyard limited for the acquisition
of 8 next generation corvettes for the Indian Navy.
The contracts were inked in the presence of Defence Secretary Rajesh Kumar Singh in New
Delhi.
Under the contracts, garden reed shipbuilders and engineers limited will construct five
corvettes, while Goa shipyard limited will construct the remaining three.
The Ministry said the project marks a significant milestone, as it is the first project in
which the ships will be indigenously designed by the inter-navy and constructed by Defence
public sector undertakings selected through a competitive process.
The construction of these ships is expected to generate approximately 72 lakh-person days
of employment in the shipyards and 460 lakh-person days in ancillary industries and MSMEs over
the next 10 years.
Defence Minister Rajnath Singh hailed the contracts signed today in a social media post.
Mr Singh described it as great news for India's indigenous shipbuilding ecosystem.
The Defence Minister Rajnath Singh met newly appointed Chief of Air Staff, Air Chief Marshal
Ashutosh Dixit.
In a social media post, Mr Singh said, Air Chief Marshal Dixit is a distinguished air
warrior known for excellent leadership.
The Defence Minister also wished him a wonderful tenure ahead.
Sitting Punjab MLA's Kuvar Vijay Pratap Singh, Harmeet Singh, Patan Majra and Chaitan
Singh Jor Majra, today joined the BJP at the party headquarters in New Delhi.
They joined the party in the presence of BJP General Secretary Satish Punea and Party Punjab
Unit President Keval Singh Dhillon.
They had resigned from the AAP recently.
Kover Vijay Pratap Singh, a former IPS officer, represented Amrit Sir North seat, Harmeet Singh
Pathan Majra, the Sannar seat, and Chetan Singh Jor Majra represented the Samana Assembly
constituency.
The Enforcement Directorate, ED, is conducting searches at multiple locations in Punjab and
Chandigarh in connection with a corruption and disproportionate assets case involving
former Punjab Industries Minister and Congress Leader Sundar Shyam Arora, his son Pratikar
Arora, and others.
Search operations are being carried out at premises linked to Marbella Group, Gulmohar
Township Group, their promoters, and Sanjeev Duneja.
Officials at the ED said the investigation is related to alleged corruption, irregularities
in the allotment of plots, by Punjab small industries and export cooperation and changes
in ownership of the allotted plots.
This is Aakashwani giving you the news.

Welcome back to the midday news.
The severe cyclonic storm Urusu over west-central and adjoining southwest way of Bengal moved
west-northwestwards and lay centered about 120 km east-south east of Nellore, Andhra
Pradesh and 160 km northeast of Chennai.
The Indermatological Department, IMD, has said it is very likely to move north-westwards
and cross South Antapradesh coast, with wind speed of 100 to 110 km per hour, gusting to
120 km per hour between Nellore and Narsapur during midnight tonight.
The Med Department has advised fishermen not to venture into South-East Bay of Bengal
call today. And into southwest Bay of Bengal, till Wednesday morning, Andhra Pradesh is
on high alert. A severe cyclonic storm, Murusso approaches the coast. The state government
has intensified preparedness to protect lives and property, a report.
Cyclone Murusso is likely to cross the South Andhra Pradesh coast near Vangol around midnight
tonight or during the early hours of tomorrow. Heavy to extremely heavy rainfall is forecast
in coastal districts and Raya Seema. The state government has directed officials
officials to evacuate people from low-lying areas and make arrangements for relief shelters,
drinking water, food and medical services.
Six NDRF and seven SDRF teams have been kept ready for rescue operations.
Officials have also been instructed to closely monitor roads, bridges and culverts, clear
fallen trees and prevent people from crossing flooded routes.
Reservoirs are being monitored regularly to manage possible flooding.
Electricity teams have been placed on standby with essential equipment to ensure
early restoration of power.
control rooms are functioning, and people have been advised to remain indoors and follow official warnings.
Ali Murli, Aakashwani News, Vijayawada.

The situation in southern Odisha remains a matter of serious concern, as the region still
struggling to recover from the recent floods, bases for another spell of heavy rainfall
due to severe cyclonic storm, Murasu.
Several areas in Ganjam, Gajapati and Kandamal are yet to fully recover, from the damage
caused by floods and landslides.
With rain already beginning in parts of southern Odisha, the administration is rushing
against time to move people from vulnerable locations to safer shelters. The government
has identified seven vulnerable districts, Ganjam, Gajapati, Kannamal, Kalahandi, Raigada,
Koraput and Malkangiri. Schools in vulnerable areas will remain closed tomorrow and the
day after. More than 300 rescue teams comprising NDRF, ODRAF and fire services have been deployed
for emergency operations, while people who had recently returned home after the floods
are being shifted back to cyclone centers. The immediate concern is that fresh rainfall
could ocean-flooding trigger landslides and further disrupt normal life in these already
affected districts.
Prakash Das for Akaswani News, Bhubaneswar.
The country's gross goods and services tax GST collections grew nearly 23 percent here
on year to over 231,000 crore rupees in October this year, driven by robust domestic economic
activity and a sharp rise in tax revenue from imports.
According to the Provisional Government data, gross GST revenue from domestic sales climbed
15.8% here on year to over 1.59 lakh crore rupees in October, while revenue from imports
surged 42.2% to 72,246 crore rupees. The gross GST revenue collection includes central GST
map up of 42,935 crore rupees, stayed GST of 51,340 crore rupees, and integrated GST
of 137,015 crore rupees.
National Security Advisor Jee Dupal held talks with Vietnam's Deputy Prime Minister and
Defence Minister General Van Nguyen in Hanoi, reviewing bilateral defence cooperation and
agreeing to strengthen engagement in the sector.
India.
The Embassy of India and Vietnam said in a social media post that the two leaders discussed
ongoing defence cooperation and ways to deepen ties.
Mr. Dho Bhal arrived in Hanoi yesterday for an official visit during which he is scheduled
to meet Vietnamese leaders to review the enhanced comprehensive strategic partnership between
the two countries.
In Nepal, all six Indian tourists stranded in Upper Dholpa region due to heavy snowfall
have been safely rescued and brought to Dunei.
The district administration office has confirmed that all six are in normal condition.
The tourists were airlifted by helicopter after heavy snowfall blocked trekking routes in the Dhanigarh area.
Kimi Antonelli has created history about becoming the youngest driver in F1 history.
To be crowned champion after finishing third at the Mexico City Grand Prix,
the 20-year-old Italian has secured the title for Mercedes.
Red Bulls Max Verstappen won the race as Lewis Hamilton finished second for Ferrari.
In cricket, Jammu and Kashmir beat Rajasthan in the final of the 10th T20 national championship for the deaf yesterday.
14 teams participated in the championship from different states, which marked an important milestone in the continued development of cricket for the hearing impaired in India.
The Indian Deaf Cricketer Association is expanding its reach to new regions and bringing athletes
together through structured national level competition, continuing to work towards strengthening
the sporting ecosystem for deaf cricketers and advancing greater recognition of their
talents and achievements.
And now before we end the bulletin, the headlines once again.
